question: A 49-year-old man comes to the physician for evaluation of several painless, pruritic lesions on his left forearm that he first noticed 4 days ago. They were initially pink marks that progressed into blisters before ulcerating. He has also had a headache for 1 week. His temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). A photograph of one of the lesions is shown. There is pronounced edema of the surrounding skin and painless swelling of the left axillary lymph nodes. Which of the following is the greatest risk factor for this patient's condition?
analysis: The patient's presentation with painless, pruritic lesions progressing to blisters and ulceration, along with headache, fever, edema, and lymphadenopathy, is suggestive of cutaneous anthrax. The greatest risk factor for this patient's condition is likely wool handling, as anthrax spores can be found in contaminated animal products such as wool.
